chunks: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Razi narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, saying: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, saying:
As-Sufyani was mentioned before Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he said: 'How will that come out? And when he comes out, the breaker of his eyes will be in Sana'a.'

key_terms.السُّفْيَانِيُّ: As-Sufyani, a specific figure in Shia eschatology associated with the pre-Mahdi era.
key_terms.صَنْعَاءَ: Sana'a, a city in Yemen, significant in Shia eschatological narratives.
key_terms.كَاسِرُ عَيْنَيْهِ: The breaker of his eyes, a descriptive title for a key figure in the narrative of As-Sufyani's rise.

ai.seo_question: Who is the 'breaker of his eyes' mentioned in relation to As-Sufyani's emergence?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the eschatological sign of the Sufyani, a key figure in Shia apocalyptic tradition whose emergence signals the Mahdi's advent. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies a specific counterpart, 'the breaker of his eyes' (Kasir Aynayhi), located in Sana'a, illustrating the dualistic cosmic struggle between the forces of tyranny and divine justice. This detail underscores the geographical and spiritual dimensions of the final victory, linking local historical contexts in Yemen to the universal manifestation of the Mahdi.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (60) Ali bin al-Husayn narrated from Muhammad bin Yahya al-Attar from Muhammad bin Hassaan ar-Razi from Muhammad bin Ali al-Kufi from Muhammad bin Sinan that Obayd bin Zurara had said:
“Once as-Sufyani was mentioned before Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as). He said: “He (as-Syfyani) will not rise except after the rising of the one in Sana’a.”
